Boracay.question: The OCA awarded the hosting rights to the Philippines as it had been the host of the first _____ held in Manila 100 years earlier

The OCA awarded the hosting rights to the Philippines as it had been the host of the first Far Eastern Championship Games held in Manila 100 years earlier.

Boracay.subject: Computer & IT
Boracay.question: However, it had to be rescheduled and relocated because of _____, with the ceremony eventually taking place at the Sofitel Plaza in Manila on January 17, 2014
Boracay.fact: However, it had to be rescheduled and relocated because of Typhoon Haiyan, with the ceremony eventually taking place at the Sofitel Plaza in Manila on January 17, 2014.

Boracay.fact: On March 25, 2026, DPWH Secretary Vivencio Dizon issued the Notice of Award to SMHC for the financing, design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the bridge.

Boracay.subject: Computer & IT

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The _____ was Protocol for communicating routing information on the Internet.
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is a standardized exterior gateway protocol designed to exchange routing and reachability information among autonomous systems (AS) on the Internet. BGP used for routing within an autonomous system is called Interior Border Gateway Protocol (iBGP).

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The initial BGP design was recorded on two napkins, hence often referenced to as the “Two-_____”
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The initial BGP design was recorded on two napkins, hence often referenced to as the “Two-Napkin Protocol”.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: A photocopy of these three sheets of paper now hangs on the wall of a routing protocol development area at _____ in Milpitas, California
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A photocopy of these three sheets of paper now hangs on the wall of a routing protocol development area at Cisco Systems in Milpitas, California.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In the same year, RFC _____ was published, and the BGP protocol (in various forms) has been in use on the Internet since 1994
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In the same year, RFC 1105 was published, and the BGP protocol (in various forms) has been in use on the Internet since 1994.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Half a year after the initial publication, the protocol definition was changed in _____ with the publication of RFC 1136
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Half a year after the initial publication, the protocol definition was changed in 1990 with the publication of RFC 1136.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In October _____, BGP version 3 was defined in RFC 1267, obsoleting the two earlier versions
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In October 1991, BGP version 3 was defined in RFC 1267, obsoleting the two earlier versions.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In _____, the current version (BGP4), was published as RFC 1654
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In the same year, RFC 1105 was published, and the BGP protocol (in various forms) has been in use on the Internet since 1994. In 1994, the current version (BGP4), was published as RFC 1654.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Its definition was replaced in March _____ by RFC 1771
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Its definition was replaced in March 1995 by RFC 1771.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In January _____, RFC 4271 was published, which currently is the latest definition of BGP4 (although updated by many other RFCs)
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In January 2006, RFC 4271 was published, which currently is the latest definition of BGP4 (although updated by many other RFCs).

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The major enhancement of BGP4 was the support for _____-Domain Routing (CIDR) and use of route aggregation to decrease the size of routing tables
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The major enhancement of BGP4 was the support for Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) and use of route aggregation to decrease the size of routing tables.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Since the publication of RFC 2283 in _____, routing information about a wide range of "address families" (IPv4, IPv6, IPX, etc.) can be carried
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Since the publication of RFC 2283 in 1998, routing information about a wide range of "address families" (IPv4, IPv6, IPX, etc.) can be carried.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The 'Multiprotocol Extensions' have been updated in _____ with RFC 2858 and finally in 2007 with RFC 4760
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The 'Multiprotocol Extensions' have been updated in 2000 with RFC 2858 and finally in 2007 with RFC 4760.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: With these extensions, the protocol is also referred to as _____ BGP (MP-BGP)
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The 'Multiprotocol Extensions' have been updated in 2000 with RFC 2858 and finally in 2007 with RFC 4760. With these extensions, the protocol is also called Multiprotocol BGP (MP-BGP).

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If the multiprotocol extensions to BGP are negotiated at the time of creation, the BGP speaker can prefix the _____ (NLRI) it advertises with an address family prefix
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If the multiprotocol extensions to BGP are negotiated at the time of creation, the BGP speaker can prefix the Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) it advertises with an address family prefix.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: These families include the IPv4 (default), IPv6, IPv4/IPv6 _____ and multicast BGP
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: These families include the IPv4 (default), IPv6, IPv4/IPv6 Virtual Private Networks and multicast BGP.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Increasingly, BGP is used as a generalized signaling protocol to carry information about routes that may not be part of the global _____, such as VPNs
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Increasingly, BGP is used as a generalized signaling protocol to carry information about routes that may not be part of the global Internet, such as VPNs.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In order to make decisions in its operations with peers, a BGP peer uses a simple finite-state machine (FSM) that consists of six states: Idle; _____; Active; OpenSent; OpenConfirm; and Established
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In order to make decisions in its operations with peers, a BGP peer uses a simple finite-state machine (FSM) that consists of six states: Idle; Connect; Active; OpenSent; OpenConfirm; and Established.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The first state is the _____ state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In order to make decisions in its operations with peers, a BGP peer uses a simple finite-state machine (FSM) that consists of six states: Idle; Connect; Active; OpenSent; OpenConfirm; and Established. The first state is the Idle state.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In the _____ state, BGP initializes all resources, refuses all inbound BGP connection attempts and initiates a TCP connection to the peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The first state is the Idle state. In the Idle state, BGP initializes all resources, refuses all inbound BGP connection attempts and initiates a TCP connection to the peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In the _____ state, the router waits for the TCP connection to complete and transitions to the OpenSent state if successful
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In the Idle state, BGP initializes all resources, refuses all inbound BGP connection attempts and initiates a TCP connection to the peer. The second state is Connect.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If unsuccessful, it starts the _____Retry timer and transitions to the Active state upon expiration
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In the Idle state, BGP initializes all resources, refuses all inbound BGP connection attempts and initiates a TCP connection to the peer. The second state is Connect.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In the _____ state, the router resets the ConnectRetry timer to zero and returns to the Connect state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If unsuccessful, it starts the ConnectRetry timer and transitions to the Active state upon expiration. In the Active state, the router resets the ConnectRetry timer to zero and returns to the Connect state.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In the OpenSent state, the router sends an Open message and waits for one in return in order to transition to the Open_____ state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In the OpenSent state, the router sends an Open message and waits for one in return in order to transition to the OpenConfirm state.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In the Established state, the router can send and receive: _____; Update; and Notification messages to and from its peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Keepalive messages are exchanged and, upon successful receipt, the router is placed into the Established state. In the Established state, the router can send and receive: Keepalive; Update; and Notification messages to and from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Idle State: _____ all incoming BGP connections
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Idle State: Refuse all incoming BGP connections.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The '_____' have been updated in 2000 with RFC 2858 and finally in 2007 with RFC 4760
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The 'Multiprotocol Extensions' have been updated in 2000 with RFC 2858 and finally in 2007 with RFC 4760.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Changes its state to _____
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Initiates a TCP connection with its configured BGP peer. Listens for a TCP connection from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If an error occurs at any state of the FSM process, the BGP session is terminated immediately and returned to the _____ state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If an error occurs at any state of the FSM process, the BGP session is terminated immediately and returned to the Idle state. Some of the reasons why a router does not progress from the Idle state are: TCP port 179 is not open.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Some of the reasons why a router does not progress from the _____ state are: TCP port 179 is not open
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If an error occurs at any state of the FSM process, the BGP session is terminated immediately and returned to the Idle state. Some of the reasons why a router does not progress from the Idle state are: TCP port 179 is not open.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: A random TCP port over _____ is not open
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A random TCP port over 1023 is not open.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Connect State: _____ for successful TCP negotiation with peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Connect State: Waits for successful TCP negotiation with peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Sends _____ message to peer and changes state to OpenSent
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Sends Open message to peer and changes state to OpenSent. Some reasons for the error are: TCP port 179 is not open.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If an error occurs, BGP moves to the _____ state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If an error occurs, BGP moves to the Active state.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: BGP FSM tries to restart another TCP session with the peer and, if successful, then it sends an _____ message to the peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: BGP FSM tries to restart another TCP session with the peer and, if successful, then it sends an Open message to the peer. Some of the reasons for this include: TCP port 179 is not open.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If it is unsuccessful again, the FSM is reset to the _____ state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If it is unsuccessful again, the FSM is reset to the Idle state. Repeated failures may result in a router cycling between the Idle and Active states.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Repeated failures may result in a router cycling between the Idle and _____ states
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Active State: If the router was unable to establish a successful TCP session, then it ends up in the Active state. Repeated failures may result in a router cycling between the Idle and Active states.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Open_____: BGP FSM listens for an Open message from its peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: OpenSent State: BGP FSM listens for an Open message from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Once the message has been received, the router checks the validity of the _____ message
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: OpenSent State: BGP FSM listens for an Open message from its peer. Once the message has been received, the router checks the validity of the Open message.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If there is an error, it is because one of the fields in the _____ message does not match between the peers, e.g., BGP version mismatch, the peering router expects a different My AS, etc
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: OpenSent State: BGP FSM listens for an Open message from its peer. Once the message has been received, the router checks the validity of the Open message.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The router then sends a _____ message to the peer indicating why the error occurred
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The router then sends a Notification message to the peer indicating why the error occurred.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If there is no error, a _____ message is sent, various timers are set and the state is changed to OpenConfirm
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If there is no error, a Keepalive message is sent, various timers are set and the state is changed to OpenConfirm. OpenConfirm State: The peer is listening for a Keepalive message from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If a _____ message is received and no timer has expired before reception of the Keepalive, BGP transitions to the Established state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If there is no error, a Keepalive message is sent, various timers are set and the state is changed to OpenConfirm. OpenConfirm State: The peer is listening for a Keepalive message from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If a timer expires before a _____ message is received, or if an error condition occurs, the router transitions back to the Idle state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If there is no error, a Keepalive message is sent, various timers are set and the state is changed to OpenConfirm. OpenConfirm State: The peer is listening for a Keepalive message from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Open_____: The peer is listening for a Keepalive message from its peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: OpenConfirm State: The peer is listening for a Keepalive message from its peer.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Established State: In this state, the peers send _____ messages to exchange information about each route being advertised to the BGP peer
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Established State: In this state, the peers send Update messages to exchange information about each route being advertised to the BGP peer. If there is any error in the Update message then a Notification message is sent to the peer, and BGP transitions back to the Idle state.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: If there is any error in the _____ message then a Notification message is sent to the peer, and BGP transitions back to the Idle state
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Established State: In this state, the peers send Update messages to exchange information about each route being advertised to the BGP peer. If there is any error in the Update message then a Notification message is sent to the peer, and BGP transitions back to the Idle state.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: A given BGP router may accept network-layer reachability information (_____) updates from multiple neighbors and advertise NLRI to the same, or a different set, of neighbors
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A given BGP router may accept network-layer reachability information (NLRI) updates from multiple neighbors and advertise NLRI to the same, or a different set, of neighbors. Adj-RIB-In: For each neighbor, the BGP process maintains a conceptual adjacent routing information base, incoming, containing the NLRI received from the neighbor.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Adj-RIB-In: For each neighbor, the BGP process maintains a conceptual adjacent routing information base, incoming, containing the _____ received from the neighbor
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A given BGP router may accept network-layer reachability information (NLRI) updates from multiple neighbors and advertise NLRI to the same, or a different set, of neighbors. Adj-RIB-In: For each neighbor, the BGP process maintains a conceptual adjacent routing information base, incoming, containing the NLRI received from the neighbor.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Adj-RIB-Out: For each neighbor, the BGP process maintains a conceptual adjacent routing information base, outgoing , containing the _____ sent to the neighbor
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Adj-RIB-In: For each neighbor, the BGP process maintains a conceptual adjacent routing information base, incoming, containing the NLRI received from the neighbor. Adj-RIB-Out: For each neighbor, the BGP process maintains a conceptual adjacent routing information base, outgoing , containing the NLRI sent to the neighbor.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Some of the information carried that is explicitly intended to be used in policy decisions are: _____ multi-exit discriminators (MED)
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Some of the information carried that is explicitly intended to be used in policy decisions are: Communities multi-exit discriminators (MED).

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The first decision point for evaluating _____ is that its next-hop attribute must be reachable (or resolvable)
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The first decision point for evaluating NLRI is that its next-hop attribute must be reachable (or resolvable).

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: While it is common to say that BGP allows an administrator to set policies on how prefixes are handled by _____, this is generally not possible, strictly speaking
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: While it is common to say that BGP allows an administrator to set policies on how prefixes are handled by ISPs, this is generally not possible, strictly speaking.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: For instance, BGP natively has no concept to allow one AS to tell another AS to restrict advertisement of a prefix to only _____ peering customers
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: For instance, BGP natively has no concept to allow one AS to tell another AS to restrict advertisement of a prefix to only North American peering customers.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The IANA administers the registry for BGP _____
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The IANA administers the registry for BGP Extended Communities Types.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The _____ registry therefore provides different number ranges for the attribute types
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: The IANA administers the registry for BGP Extended Communities Types. The IANA registry therefore provides different number ranges for the attribute types.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: RFC 4360 exemplarily defines the "Two-Octet AS _____", the "IPv4 Address Specific Extended Community", the "Opaque Extended Community", the "Route Target Community", and the "Route Origin Community"
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: RFC 4360 exemplarily defines the "Two-Octet AS Specific Extended Community", the "IPv4 Address Specific Extended Community", the "Opaque Extended Community", the "Route Target Community", and the "Route Origin Community".

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: A number of _____ drafts also use this Extended Community Attribute structure for inter-domain QoS signalling
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A number of BGP QoS drafts also use this Extended Community Attribute structure for inter-domain QoS signalling.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Since _____, extended communities are compatible with 32-bit ASNs
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Since 2014, extended communities are compatible with 32-bit ASNs.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: To accommodate 32-bit AS numbers in _____, a Large Community attribute of 12 bytes was defined, divided in three field of 4 bytes each (AS:function:parameter)
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: To accommodate 32-bit AS numbers in BGP Communities, a Large Community attribute of 12 bytes was defined, divided in three field of 4 bytes each (AS:function:parameter).

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Another application of _____ is to advertise the value, typically based on delay, of multiple ASs that have a presence at an IXP, that they impose to send traffic to some destination
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Another application of MEDs is to advertise the value, typically based on delay, of multiple ASs that have a presence at an IXP, that they impose to send traffic to some destination.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Some routers (like _____) will use the Metric from OSPF to set MED
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Some routers (like Juniper) will use the Metric from OSPF to set MED.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Marker: 128 bits _____ for compatibility, MUST be set to all ones
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Marker: 128 bits Included for compatibility, MUST be set to all ones.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Length: 16 bits _____ length of the message in octets, including the header
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Length: 16 bits Total length of the message in octets, including the header.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: My AS: 16 bits _____ autonomous system number
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: My AS: 16 bits Senders autonomous system number.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Hold Time: 16 bits _____ timer, used to calculate KeepAlive messages
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Hold Time: 16 bits Timeout timer, used to calculate KeepAlive messages.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: BGP _____: 32 bits Holds the IP address of the sender
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: BGP Identifier: 32 bits Holds the IP address of the sender.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Parameters Length: 8 bits _____ length of the Parameters field in octets
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Parameters Length: 8 bits Total length of the Parameters field in octets.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Parameters: variable _____ parameters
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Parameters: variable Optional parameters.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: A list of all capabilities is maintained by _____
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A list of all capabilities is maintained by IANA.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Withdrawn Routes _____: 16 bits Length of the following withdrawn routes
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Withdrawn Routes Length: 16 bits Length of the following withdrawn routes. Withdrawn Routes: variable A list of withdrawn routes, specified as a series of <length, prefix> tuples.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Total Path Attribute _____: 16 bits Length of the following path attributes
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Withdrawn Routes Length: 16 bits Length of the following withdrawn routes. Withdrawn Routes: variable A list of withdrawn routes, specified as a series of <length, prefix> tuples.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: The length of this field can be caclulated as: Length - 23 - Withdrawn Routes Length - _____
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Total Path Attribute Length: 16 bits Length of the following path attributes. The length of this field can be caclulated as: Length - 23 - Withdrawn Routes Length - Total Path Attribute Length.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Data: variable _____ data to help diagnose the problem
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Data: variable Optional data to help diagnose the problem.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Before making use of this feature, the capability '_____ (2)' should be specified in the 'Open' message
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Before making use of this feature, the capability 'Route Refresh Capability (2)' should be specified in the 'Open' message. Fine-grained routing updates may be acquired when the capability 'Enhanced Route Refresh Capability (70)' is also given.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Fine-grained routing updates may be acquired when the capability '_____ (70)' is also given
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Fine-grained routing updates may be acquired when the capability 'Enhanced Route Refresh Capability (70)' is also given.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Address Family Identifier (AFI): 16 bits An identifier for the address family (IPv4, IPv6, IPX, _____Talk, etc.) This list is maintained by IANA
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Address Family Identifier (AFI): 16 bits An identifier for the address family (IPv4, IPv6, IPX, AppleTalk, etc.) This list is maintained by IANA.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: Subsequent Address Family Identifier: 8 bit This field provides additional information about the type of the _____ (NLRI) carried in the attribute
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: Subsequent Address Family Identifier: 8 bit This field provides additional information about the type of the Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) carried in the attribute.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: This approach, similar to _____'s DR/BDR feature, provides large networks with added iBGP scalability
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: This approach, similar to OSPF's DR/BDR feature, provides large networks with added iBGP scalability.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: An RR topology can cut these 90 statements down to 18, offering a viable solution for the larger networks administered by _____
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: An RR topology can cut these 90 statements down to 18, offering a viable solution for the larger networks administered by ISPs.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: In common practice, only one of the confederation AS numbers is seen by the _____ as a whole
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In common practice, only one of the confederation AS numbers is seen by the Internet as a whole.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: On the _____, a BGP routing change may cause outages for several minutes
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: On the Internet, a BGP routing change may cause outages for several minutes.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: This has led the RIPE _____ to write, "With the current implementations of BGP flap damping, the application of flap damping in ISP networks is NOT recommended
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: This has led the RIPE Routing Working Group to write, "With the current implementations of BGP flap damping, the application of flap damping in ISP networks is NOT recommended.

Border Gateway Protocol.fact: If flap damping is implemented, the ISP operating that network will cause side-effects to their customers and the Internet users of their customers' content and services ... Border Gateway Protocol.question: In an attempt to prevent this, ISPs cooperated in keeping the global routing table as small as possible by using _____-Domain Routing (CIDR) and route aggregation
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: In an attempt to prevent this, ISPs cooperated in keeping the global routing table as small as possible by using Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) and route aggregation.

Border Gateway Protocol.fact: While this slowed the growth of the routing table to a linear process for several years, with the expanded demand for multihoming by end-user networks, the growth was once again superlinear by the middle of 2004.

Border Gateway Protocol.fact: While a full IPv4 BGP table as of August 2014 (512k day) was in excess of 512,000 prefixes, many older routers had a limit of 512k (512,000–524,288) routing table entries. Border Gateway Protocol.fact: While a full IPv4 BGP table as of August 2014 (512k day) was in excess of 512,000 prefixes, many older routers had a limit of 512k (512,000–524,288) routing table entries. On August 12, 2014, outages resulting from full tables hit eBay, LastPass and Microsoft Azure, among others.

Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A number of Cisco routers commonly in use had TCAM, a form of high-speed content-addressable memory, for storing BGP advertised routes.

Border Gateway Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Border Gateway Protocol.question: On impacted routers, the _____ was by default allocated as 512k IPv4 routes and 256k IPv6 routes
Border Gateway Protocol.fact: A number of Cisco routers commonly in use had TCAM, a form of high-speed content-addressable memory, for storing BGP advertised routes. On impacted routers, the TCAM was by default allocated as 512k IPv4 routes and 256k IPv6 routes.

Cartan–Dieudonné theorem.question: The _____ was Mathematic theorem.
Cartan–Dieudonné theorem.fact: In mathematics, the Cartan–Dieudonné theorem, named after Élie Cartan and Jean Dieudonné, establishes that every orthogonal transformation in an n-dimensional symmetric bilinear space can be described as the composition of at most n reflections.

Cartan–Dieudonné theorem.subject: Computer & IT
Cartan–Dieudonné theorem.question: Similarly, in three-dimensional _____ space, every orthogonal transformation can be described as a single reflection, a rotation (2 reflections), or an improper rotation (3 reflections)
Cartan–Dieudonné theorem.fact: For example, in the two-dimensional Euclidean plane, every orthogonal transformation is either a reflection across a line through the origin or a rotation about the origin (which can be written as the composition of two reflections). Similarly, in three-dimensional Euclidean space, every orthogonal transformation can be described as a single reflection, a rotation (2 reflections), or an improper rotation (3 reflections).
